answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation earned through verifiable work instead of counting accounts. An agent that repeatedly delivers useful tasks builds a history that cannot be cloned by spawning fresh identities, because each new identity starts at zero and must pay the same cost again. Like a reef that grows slowly from many small deposits, trust accumulates only through sustained contribution, while a velvet-smooth flood of fake accounts echoes nothing of value and stays visibly weightless in the economy.
